claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'd like to ask you a few more questions about Alex to determine your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, sixth form, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure actually - he might have left or might still be in something, I haven't really kept track of exactly what his status is right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that's an important detail we need to clarify. Let me ask a different question that might help:

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask another important question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't get any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now, to help determine Alex's eligibility, I need to understand his education/training status a bit better.

**Can you find out whether Alex is currently enrolled in any form of education or training?** This could include:
- School or sixth form
- College courses
- A levels or similar qualifications
- Vocational training
- Any other approved education or training program

This is important because for a 16-year-old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I really can't say for certain - I honestly don't know if he's enrolled in anything at the moment or not. His situation might have changed recently and I'm just not clear on the details.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - thank you for being honest about what you know and don't know about Alex's current situation.

Let me ask a few more questions to complete my assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And one final question:

**Do you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000 per year?** (This won't affect whether you're eligible for Child Benefit, but it may affect whether you need to pay a tax charge.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that - I'm just trying to find out if I can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 16 years old, the key factor for Child Benefit eligibility is **whether he is in approved education or training**. The rules state that you can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training.

The good news is that:
- Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
- Alex is not claiming benefits in his own right
- He lives with you in the UK

These factors would not disqualify you. However, **without knowing whether Alex is currently enrolled in approved education or training, I cannot determine if you're eligible**.

**What you should do:**

1. Find out whether Alex is currently enrolled in any education or training (school, college, sixth form, vocational training, etc.)
2. Once you have this information, you can either:
   - Contact the Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your situation
   - Come back with this information and I can give you a definitive answer

If Alex is in approved education or training, you would likely be eligible. If he's not, you would generally not be eligible unless he registers with a careers service or the armed services (in which case you could claim for up to 20 weeks).
